title: Avicularin inhibits ferroptosis and improves cognitive impairments in Alzheimer's disease by modulating the NOX4/Nrf2 axis.
authors: Li, Zixiang; Lu, Yingying; Zhen, Yongqi; Jin, Wenke; Ma, Xuelan; Yuan, Ziyue; Liu, Bo; Zhou, Xian-Li; Zhang, Lan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Avicularin通过NOX4/Nrf2轴抑制铁死亡改善阿尔茨海默病认知障碍，核心为神经药理学机制，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a widespread neurodegenerative disorder for which effective therapies remain elusive, primarily due to the complexity of its underlying pathophysiology. In recent years, natural products have gained attention for their therapeutic potential in AD, owing to their multi-targeted actions and low toxicity profiles. Avicularin (Avi), a flavonoid derived from the peels of Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim., has shown promise as an anti-AD agent. However, the specific mechanisms by which Avi mitigates oxidative stress and inhibits ferroptosis in AD models remain insufficiently understood. Further investigation is required to elucidate its therapeutic potential in these pathways. PURPOSE: Therefore, this study aims to elucidate the neuroprotective effects of Avi in AD by investigating its impact on the NOX4/Nrf2 signaling pathway, as well as its role in modulating oxidative stress and ferroptosis. METHODS: In this study, an in vitro H(2)O(2)-induced oxidative stress model in SH-SY5Y cells was utilized to evaluate the pharmacological efficacy and underlying mechanisms of Avi. Molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay and bio-layer interferometry assays were conducted to identify potential molecular targets of Avi. Additionally, in vivo models, including scopolamine (SCOP)-induced and APP/PS1 transgenic mice, were employed to assess the cognitive effects of Avi and further explore its associated molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Our study demonstrates that Avi effectively attenuates H(2)O(2)-induced toxicity in SH-SY5Y cells by reducing apoptosis and enhancing cellular antioxidant defenses. This neuroprotective effect is mediated through the inhibition of NOX4 and the promotion of Nrf2 nuclear translocation. Furthermore, Avi improves cognitive function and mitigates ferroptosis in both SCOP-induced and APP/PS1 transgenic mouse models of AD. CONCLUSION: Avi emerges as an effective neuroprotective agent against AD, offering a promising therapeutic approach by targeting the NOX4/Nrf2 signaling axis to alleviate oxidative stress and ferroptosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种广泛存在的神经退行性疾病，其有效疗法仍难以实现，主要归因于其潜在病理生理学的复杂性。近年来，天然产物因其多靶点作用和低毒性特征，在AD治疗潜力方面受到关注。Avicularin（Avi），一种源自花椒（Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim.）果皮中的黄酮类化合物，已显示出作为抗AD药物的前景。然而，Avi在AD模型中缓解氧化应激和抑制铁死亡（ferroptosis）的具体机制仍未被充分理解。需要进一步研究以阐明其在这些通路中的治疗潜力。目的：因此，本研究旨在通过探讨Avi对NOX4/Nrf2信号通路的影响，以及其在调节氧化应激和铁死亡中的作用，阐明Avi在AD中的神经保护效应。方法：在本研究中，利用体外H(2)O(2)诱导的SH-SY5Y细胞氧化应激模型，评估Avi的药理功效和潜在机制。采用分子对接（molecular docking）、细胞热位移分析（cellular thermal shift assay）和生物层干涉法（bio-layer interferometry）实验，以识别Avi的潜在分子靶点。此外，使用体内模型，包括东莨菪碱（scopolamine, SCOP）诱导和APP/PS1转基因小鼠，评估Avi的认知效应，并进一步探讨其相关分子机制。结果：我们的研究表明，Avi通过减少凋亡和增强细胞抗氧化防御，有效减轻H(2)O(2)诱导的SH-SY5Y细胞毒性。这种神经保护效应通过抑制NOX4和促进Nrf2核转位介导。此外，Avi在SCOP诱导和APP/PS1转基因AD小鼠模型中改善认知功能并缓解铁死亡。结论：Avi作为针对AD的有效神经保护剂，通过靶向NOX4/Nrf2信号轴以减轻氧化应激和铁死亡，提供了一种有前景的治疗方法。
